$doc: The lobby dart minigame. Deliberately its OWN file rather than a block in items.json: a dart shares its maths with a thrown flask and nothing else, and every number here is tuned against a board four metres away rather than against a corridor. Tuning one must never move the other.

throw.$doc: Flight. Faster and much flatter than an item throw (items.json -> defaults.throw), because there is no aim arc here to read the drop off. All you have is a crosshair, so the drop has to be small enough to learn in three throws.
throw.$releaseHeightOffset: Relative to the eye, as for throwables - but ZERO here, deliberately. A throwable is aimed down a drawn arc, so releasing from below the eye costs you nothing; a dart is aimed down a crosshair, and every centimetre of offset is a centimetre the crosshair lies by on top of the drop. Tested at -0.12 and every dart landed 17 cm low: 5 cm of honest ballistics and 12 cm of nothing.

wind.$doc: A draught across the annex. It is HIDDEN - nothing on screen ever shows it - and it is the entire difficulty of the minigame: far too weak to make you miss the board, quite strong enough to cost you the bull if you do not read where your last three landed.
wind.$note: A lateral ACCELERATION rather than a velocity, so a longer throw drifts further and the compensation you learn is a real one. Two sine terms per axis with periods that do not divide each other, so it drifts continuously and never settles into a pattern worth memorising. At 3.2 m/s^2 over a 0.14 s flight that is about 3 cm of drift - five times the radius of the inner bull, twice the radius of the 25, and a seventh of the radius of the board. So: the bull is a real prize, and the board is never in danger.
wind.$verticalScale: The up-and-down component, as a fraction of the sideways one. Weaker, because it lands on top of the drop the player is already compensating for.

board.$doc: Regulation. Every ring is a FRACTION of `radius`, and art/shared/lobby/textures.ts paints the same fractions - so the picture and the scoring cannot disagree about where a treble is.
board.$sectors: Clockwise from the top, starting with the bed at twelve o'clock.

stick.$doc: How long a dart stays where it landed, and how many are drawn at once before the oldest is pulled out. Nothing about this is simulated once a dart has landed - it is a model sitting in a hole.

hand.$doc: The dart held ready while the button is down, in the camera's own frame: right of the crosshair, below it, and forward. There is no aim arc - this IS the aim feedback.
